findings.claim: No test covers the order 'unknown id before no-field' (edit with an unknown id and no option), which AC-4 and the plan's risks state.
findings.failure_scenario: If edit_task checked 'nothing to edit' before looking up the id, `edit 99` would print `error: nothing to edit` instead of `error: no task with id 99` and every test would still pass, because the unknown-id cases always pass --title or --priority.
findings.evidence: assert_error(path, capsys, before, "error: no task with id 99", "edit", "99", "--title", "x")

defenses.quote:
assert_error(path, capsys, before, None, "edit", "1")
    assert_error(path, capsys, before, "error: no task with id 99", "edit", "99", "--title", "x")
    # an unknown id is reported before a bad value
    assert_error(path, capsys, before, "error: no task with id 99", "edit", "99", "--priority", "urgent")
defenses.reason: The test file lacks a test case for edit with an unknown ID and no field options. The function test_ac4_no_field_and_unknown_id_are_errors tests edit 1 with no options (line 102), edit 99 with --title (line 103), and edit 99 with --priority (line 105), but does not test edit 99 with no field options. This gap means the test suite would not catch a regression if the check order were changed to report 'nothing to edit' before checking if the ID exists.

gaps.detail: No test applies several valid options in one edit (e.g. `edit 1 --title X --no-due --priority low`, or --title with --due and --priority). Add a CLI test in tests/test_edit.py checking all fields change together and the other keys (done, tags) and other tasks stay intact.

AC-4 says an unknown id is reported before value errors, but `edit 99 --due 2026-12-01 --no-due` (unknown id with the due/no-due conflict) is untested. In core.edit_task the due/no-due check could move before _find unnoticed. Add this case to test_ac4_no_field_and_unknown_id_are_errors, expecting 'error: no task with id 99'. (The `edit 99` no-option case is already finding tests-1.)

Strictness of --priority and --due inputs is not pinned by any test: `--priority HIGH`, `--priority ' high'`, `--priority ''`, and `--due ' 2026-12-01'` or a non-ASCII-digit date are rejected by the PRIORITIES membership check and by parse_date, but only urgent, 2026-02-30, abc and the empty due string are tested. Add parametrized invalid-priority and invalid-due cases expecting the exact 'error: invalid priority: X' / 'error: invalid due date: X' and an unchanged file.
